gloss: seek, look for; seek to do; require; ask, request
summary: To look for what is absent or lost so as to find it, and so to seek after, try to get, or ask for. Scripture uses it almost only in the piel: of a man seeking his brothers or his father's asses, of enemies who “seek the life” of David or Elijah, of Israel seeking Yahweh and his face, which promises that those who seek him with all the heart will find him (Deu 4:29), and, with מִיַּד “from the hand of”, of requiring a life or blood back from someone answerable for it. The noun בַּקָּשָׁה is a request made to a king, beside שְׁאֵלָה “petition”. Ugaritic bqṯ “search” and Phoenician bqš “look for; request” are the same root.

words.gloss: seek, look for; seek out, try to get; seek to do; seek Yahweh; require; request
words.summary: About 225 times, all but three in the piel. Its constant partner is מָצָא “find”: seeking aims at finding, and “he sought and did not find” is the commonest way the text says something is gone (1Sa 10:21; 2Ki 2:17; Psa 37:36; Sng 3:1). It overlaps דָּרַשׁ “inquire of, seek”, beside which it stands in Deu 4:29, Psa 105:4 and Ezk 34:6. The pual is the passive, “be sought”, and again the sought thing is not found (Jer 50:20; Ezk 26:21).

stems.gloss: seek, look for; seek out, try to get; seek to do; seek Yahweh; require, exact; ask, request

senses.definition: To look for a person or thing that is missing, lost or hidden, in order to find it; the outcome, found or not found, is usually told with מָצָא.

evidence.note: Joseph wandering in the field: “What are you seeking (תְּבַקֵּשׁ)?” “My brothers I am seeking (מְבַקֵּשׁ); tell me where they are pasturing.”
Kish sends Saul to look for the lost asses.
Saul is taken by lot, “and they sought him (וַיְבַקְשֻׁהוּ), and he was not found”.
Fifty men “sought (וַיְבַקְשׁוּ) three days, and did not find him”: Elijah.
The wicked passed away: “I sought him (וָאֲבַקְשֵׁהוּ), and he was not found.”
“I sought him whom my soul loves; I sought him and did not find him.”
“Where has your beloved turned? And we will seek him with you.”
“Seek in her squares, if you can find a man who does justice.”
“I sought from among them a man to build up the wall and stand in the breach … and I did not find.”
The shepherds of Israel “have not sought (בִקַּשְׁתֶּם) the lost (הָאֹבֶדֶת)”.
Yahweh: “The lost I will seek (אֲבַקֵּשׁ), and the strayed I will bring back.”
“I have gone astray like a lost sheep; seek (בַּקֵּשׁ) your servant.”
“These sought their register … and they were not found.”
Understanding: “if you seek her as silver, and search for her as for hidden treasures”.

senses.gloss: seek out, try to get; seek after
senses.definition: To look for someone or something one does not yet have, so as to get it: a man or a woman for a task, food, rest, a place; and of what a person sets himself after, peace, knowledge, good or evil.

evidence.note: “Yahweh has sought (בִּקֵּשׁ) for himself a man according to his heart, and Yahweh has commanded him to be ruler over his people.” Paul gives the outcome: “I have found (εὗρον) David” (Act 13:22).
“I have found David the son of Jesse, a man after my heart, who will do all my will.”
“Let them seek out a man who knows how to play the lyre.”
“Let them seek for my lord the king a young woman, a virgin, and let her stand before the king.”
“My daughter, shall I not seek rest for you, that it may be well with you?”
“All her people groan, seeking bread.”
“The young lions roar for prey, and to seek their food from God.”
“The poor and needy seek water, and there is none.”
The tribe of the Danites “was seeking for itself an inheritance to dwell in”.
They went “to seek pasture for their flocks”.
“Turn from evil and do good; seek (בַּקֵּשׁ) peace, and pursue it (וְרָדְפֵהוּ)”: seeking set beside pursuing. Quoted at 1Pe 3:11.
“Let him seek (ζητησάτω) peace and pursue it.”
“He who diligently seeks good seeks favour; but he who searches for evil, it will come to him.”
“The heart of the understanding seeks knowledge.”
“The ear of the wise seeks knowledge.”
“The lips of a priest keep knowledge, and they seek law (תוֹרָה) from his mouth.”
To Korah and the Levites: “and you seek the priesthood also”.
“And you, do you seek great things for yourself? Do not seek them.”
“God made man upright, but they have sought out many schemes.”
“Many seek the face of a ruler, but a man's judgment is from Yahweh”: seeking a man's favour.
“All the earth sought the face of Solomon, to hear his wisdom.”
“Do not turn to the mediums and the spiritists; do not seek them out, to be defiled by them.”
Saul: “Seek for me a woman who is a medium, that I may go to her and inquire (וְאֶדְרְשָׁה) of her.”

senses.definition: To turn to Yahweh and look to him: to come to him to inquire, to pray and humble oneself before him, and to give oneself to him with the whole heart. With פָּנִים, “seek the face”, to come before him for his favour. Those who seek him so are promised that they will find him.

evidence.note: “From there you will seek (וּבִקַּשְׁתֶּם) Yahweh your God, and you will find him, if you seek him (תִדְרְשֶׁנּוּ) with all your heart and with all your soul.”
“You will seek me and find me, when you seek me (תִדְרְשֻׁנִי) with all your heart.”
“Everyone who sought (מְבַקֵּשׁ) Yahweh went out to the tent of meeting”: going to inquire of him at the place he met Moses.
In the famine “David sought the face of Yahweh”, and Yahweh answered him.
“To you my heart said, Seek my face; your face, Yahweh, I will seek.”
“Seek (דִּרְשׁוּ) Yahweh and his strength; seek (בַּקְּשׁוּ) his face continually” (1Ch 16:11).
“If my people … humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their evil ways, then I will hear from heaven and forgive.”
“In their distress they turned to Yahweh the God of Israel, and sought him, and he was found by them.”
“With all their desire they sought him, and he was found by them, and Yahweh gave them rest round about.”
A fast “to humble ourselves before our God, to seek from him a straight way”.
“The hand of our God is on all who seek him (מְבַקְשָׁיו) for good, and his power and his anger against all who forsake him (עֹזְבָיו).”
“I set my face to the Lord God, to seek by prayer and supplications, with fasting and sackcloth and ashes.”
“I will return to my place until they acknowledge their guilt and seek my face; in their distress they will earnestly seek me.”
With flocks and herds they go to seek Yahweh, but do not find him: he has withdrawn from them.
“Afterward the sons of Israel will return and seek Yahweh their God and David their king.”
“Those who turned back from following Yahweh, and who have not sought Yahweh nor inquired of him.”
“Seek Yahweh, all you humble of the earth … seek righteousness, seek humility; perhaps you will be hidden in the day of the anger of Yahweh.”
“I did not say to the seed of Jacob, Seek me in vain (תֹּהוּ).”
“Listen to me, you who pursue righteousness, who seek Yahweh.”
“I was found by those who did not seek me (בִקְשֻׁנִי)”: Paul applies it to the nations (Rom 10:20).
“I was found by those who did not seek (ζητοῦσιν) me.”
“Many peoples and strong nations will come to seek Yahweh of hosts in Jerusalem.”
“The Lord whom you seek will suddenly come to his temple”, parallel to “the messenger of the covenant, in whom you delight”.
“Those who seek Yahweh understand everything.”
Paul: that they “should seek the Lord, if perhaps they might feel after him and find him”.

senses.definition: With an infinitive or a clause: to set oneself to do something, to try or intend it, whether or not it is done.

evidence.note: “Pharaoh heard this thing, and sought to kill Moses; and Moses fled.”
“Yahweh met him and sought to put him to death.”
“Saul sought to strike David to the wall with the spear, but he slipped away.”
Two eunuchs “sought to lay a hand on King Ahasuerus”.
Haman “sought to destroy all the Jews”.
“The king sought to put him to death.”
“The Preacher sought to find (בִּקֵּשׁ … לִמְצֹא) words of delight.”
“I sought understanding (וָאֲבַקְשָׁה בִינָה)”: tried to understand the vision.
“In that day I will seek to destroy all the nations that come against Jerusalem.”
Samson “was seeking an occasion against the Philistines”, and it was from Yahweh.

senses.definition: בִּקֵּשׁ נֶפֶשׁ, “seek the life (soul) of” someone, is to try to kill him; “seek the harm (רָעָה) of” someone is to plot his hurt.

evidence.note: “Return to Egypt, for all the men who sought your life (הַמְבַקְשִׁים אֶת־נַפְשֶׁךָ) are dead”: the words of Mat 2:20.
“Those who sought (ζητοῦντες) the young child's life are dead.”
“What is my sin before your father, that he seeks my life?”
“Saul had come out to seek his life.”
“I, I alone am left, and they seek my life, to take it”: quoted at Rom 11:3.
“I alone am left, and they seek (ζητοῦσιν) my life.”
The men of Anathoth, “who seek your life, saying, Do not prophesy in the name of Yahweh”.
“I will not give you into the hand of these men who seek your life.”
“Let them be ashamed … who seek my life to destroy it.”
“Those who seek my life to destroy it will go into the lower parts of the earth.”
“Why do you listen to the words of men saying, Behold, David seeks your harm (רָעָתֶךָ)?”
“Let them be covered with reproach … who seek my harm.”
Haman “stood to request for his life (לְבַקֵּשׁ עַל־נַפְשׁוֹ) from Esther”: the phrase turned round, pleading for one's own life.

senses.definition: With מִיַּד “from the hand of”: to demand back from the one answerable for it what was lost or taken, a life, blood, a pledge; to hold him to account. Without it, to demand or exact.

evidence.note: Jacob to Laban: “I bore the loss of it; from my hand you required it (תְּבַקְשֶׁנָּה), stolen by day or stolen by night.”
Judah: “I will be surety for him; from my hand you shall require him (תְּבַקְשֶׁנּוּ). If I do not bring him back to you … I will bear the blame for ever.”
“Shall I not now require his blood (אֲבַקֵּשׁ אֶת־דָּמוֹ) from your hand, and remove you from the earth?”
The watchman who does not warn the wicked: “he shall die in his iniquity, but his blood I will require from your hand.”
“And Yahweh require it from the hand of David's enemies.”
If the altar was built to turn from Yahweh, “Yahweh himself require it”.
“When you come to appear before me, who has required this from your hand, to trample my courts?”
“We will restore, and will require nothing from them.”
“I did not demand the governor's bread, because the bondage was heavy on this people.”
“That the blood of all the prophets … may be required (ἐκζητηθῇ) of this generation”: the requiring of blood.

senses.definition: To ask something of someone, above all of a king or governor: to make request for oneself or for others.

evidence.note: Mordecai charges Esther “to go in to the king to make supplication (לְהִתְחַנֶּן) to him and to make request (וּלְבַקֵּשׁ) before him for her people”.
Haman “stood to make request for his life from Esther the queen”.
“He requested (וַיְבַקֵּשׁ) of the chief of the eunuchs that he might not defile himself.”
The king: “For what do you make request (מְבַקֵּשׁ)?” “And I prayed to the God of heaven.”
“We fasted and besought (וַנְּבַקְשָׁה) our God for this, and he was entreated for us.”
Sanballat was displeased “that a man had come to seek the welfare of the sons of Israel”.
“They will seek a vision from the prophet”: ask it of him, and not get it.

senses.definition: The passive: to be looked for. Twice it is said of what is sought and is not found, gone for good; once of a matter looked into and found true.

evidence.note: “In those days … the iniquity of Israel will be sought (יְבֻקַּשׁ), and there will be none, and the sins of Judah, and they will not be found; for I will forgive those whom I leave.”
Of Tyre: “you will be sought, but you will never be found again.”
“The matter was searched out and found to be so, and both of them were hanged on a tree.”

greek.gloss: seek, look for; seek to do; ask for

evidence.locator: Gen.37.16, מְבַקֵּשׁ → ζητῶ; Exo.4.19, הַמְבַקְשִׁים → ζητοῦντες; Psa.34.15, בַּקֵּשׁ → ζήτησον; Ezk.34.16, אֲבַקֵּשׁ → ζητήσω; ζητέω renders בָּקַשׁ ×144

evidence.note: “Let him seek (ζητησάτω) peace and pursue it”: Psa 34:15.
“Those who sought (ζητοῦντες) the child's life are dead”: the words of Exo 4:19.
“They seek (ζητοῦσιν) my life”: 1Ki 19:10.
“I was found by those who did not seek (ζητοῦσιν) me”: Isa 65:1.
“The Son of man came to seek (ζητῆσαι) and to save the lost (τὸ ἀπολωλός)”: the work of the shepherd of Ezk 34:16.
“Seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness.”

evidence.locator: Ezk.3.18, אֲבַקֵּשׁ → ἐκζητήσω; Ezk.3.20, אֲבַקֵּשׁ → ἐκζητήσω; ἐκζητέω renders בָּקַשׁ ×11

evidence.note: “That the blood of all the prophets … may be required (ἐκζητηθῇ) of this generation”: the require of Ezk 3:18; 2Sa 4:11.
“He is a rewarder of those who seek him out (ἐκζητοῦσιν).”

parallels.note: “Inquire of, seek”: set beside בָּקַשׁ of seeking Yahweh, and of the shepherd seeking the flock.
“Find”: the end seeking aims at, told as found or not found.
“Ask”: the one asks of Yahweh, the other seeks him.

opposites.note: “Forsake”: those who seek Yahweh against those who forsake him.

phrases.gloss: seek someone's life: try to kill him
seek the face of: come before for favour
require from the hand of: hold answerable
sought and did not find: gone, no more

words.summary: Eight times, all in Esther and Ezra, of a request made to the Persian king, seven times paired with שְׁאֵלָה “petition”.

senses.definition: What one asks of a king: the thing sought from him.

evidence.note: “What is your request (בַּקָּשָׁתֵךְ)? Even to half the kingdom it shall be given you.”
“My petition (שְׁאֵלָתִי) and my request (וּבַקָּשָׁתִי): if I have found favour … to grant my petition and to do my request.”
“Let my life be given me at my petition, and my people at my request (בְּבַקָּשָׁתִי)”: what she asked for was her people's life.
“The king granted him all his request, according to the hand of Yahweh his God upon him.”

parallels.note: “Petition, what is asked”: the fixed partner of בַּקָּשָׁה in Esther.

cognates.note: Ugaritic writes ṯ where Hebrew has ש: the Hebrew shin here stands for older ṯ. Its sense, search, is the Hebrew's seek to find.

evidence.note: The Proto-Semitic root *bqṯ “seek”, with Hebrew baqaš (HEB001160), Punic bqš “request” (PUN000429) and Ugaritic bqṯ “search”.
Compares Ugaritic 𐎁𐎖𐎘 (bqṯ) “to search for, investigate”.

cognates.note: The same two sides as the Hebrew, looking for and asking for. On the coffin of Eshmunazor of Sidon: “let him not look for (ybqš) anything in it, for nothing has been placed in it”, the Hebrew piel's sense; and a woman's name bqšt, “requested”.

evidence.note: “[Heb. b-q-š] v. qal REQUEST”: Benz 100 (Ph), the feminine personal name bqšt, “Requested <of God>”; “v. piʿel SEEK, LOOK FOR”: KAI 14.4/5 (Ph) wʾl ybqš bn mnm, “and let him not look for anything in it”; IRT 892.3/5 (NPu), “Gaius sought favor from Dubren, his god.”

doctrine.statement: Moses told Israel that when they were scattered among the nations, “from there you will seek Yahweh your God, and you will find him, if you seek him with all your heart and with all your soul” (Deu 4:29), and Yahweh said the same to the exiles in Babylon (Jer 29:13). The history bears it out: Judah “in their distress turned to Yahweh … and sought him, and he was found by them”, and when they sought him “with all their desire … Yahweh gave them rest” (2Ch 15:4, 15). Seeking Yahweh is shown to be humbling oneself, praying, seeking his face and turning from evil ways (2Ch 7:14; Dan 9:3), and it stands against forsaking him (Ezr 8:22). Yahweh “did not say to the seed of Jacob, Seek me in vain” (Isa 45:19); yet he can withdraw from those who seek him with sacrifices and not with the heart (Hos 5:6). He was also found by those who did not seek him (Isa 65:1), which Paul applies to the nations called through the gospel (Rom 10:20), and he told the Athenians that God made the nations “that they should seek the Lord, if perhaps they might feel after him and find him” (Act 17:27); “he is a rewarder of those who seek him out” (Heb 11:6). From the verses: God is found by those who seek him with the whole heart, and he has made himself findable to Israel and to the nations alike.

Hosea foretold that Israel would live “many days without king or prince”, and “afterward the sons of Israel will return and seek Yahweh their God and David their king, and will come in fear to Yahweh and to his goodness in the latter days” (Hos 3:4–5): a king of David's line over a returned Israel. Jeremiah says that “in those days” Israel and Judah together will come weeping and seek Yahweh their God, and ask the way to Zion, to join themselves to him in an everlasting covenant; then “the iniquity of Israel will be sought, and there will be none”, because Yahweh forgives them (Jer 50:4–5, 20). Zechariah adds the nations: “many peoples and strong nations will come to seek Yahweh of hosts in Jerusalem” (Zec 8:22), after Yahweh has said, “in that day I will seek to destroy all the nations that come against Jerusalem” (Zec 12:9). Ezekiel's shepherd who seeks the lost is Yahweh himself, who sets over the flock “one shepherd, my servant David” (Ezk 34:16, 23), and Jesus, the son of David to whom God will give “the throne of his father David” (Luk 1:32), said he came “to seek and to save the lost” (Luk 19:10) and told his disciples to “seek first the kingdom of God” (Mat 6:33). From the verses: the seeking these prophets foretell is in Jerusalem, of Yahweh and of David's son as king, on the earth, in the latter days.

Judah offered himself as surety for Benjamin with the words “from my hand you shall require him” (Gen 43:9), and David said of Ish-bosheth's murderers, “shall I not require his blood from your hand?” (2Sa 4:11). Yahweh uses the same words of the watchman: if he does not warn the wicked, “he shall die in his iniquity, but his blood I will require from your hand” (Ezk 3:18, 20; 33:8). Jesus spoke of the blood of all the prophets being “required of this generation” (Luk 11:50–51). From the verses: one who is set to warn or to keep another is answerable to God for that life.

note: Drafted 2026-11-18. Root key בקש; b.cv.aa (verb, piel 222 and pual 3 tokens) and b.cv.ab (בַּקָּשָׁה) are assigned here. b.cv.ac, BDB's בַּר “son” (Psa 2:12; Pro 31:2) filed under this root, already belongs to ben.json and is left there; its double-filed tokens of בַּר “grain” (Amo 5:11; 8:6; Psa 72:16) and בְּרִי “moisture” (Job 37:11) are not this root either. No proper names are formed from the root in scripture (none in TIPNR). No Biblical Aramaic word: Daniel and Ezra, and the Peshitta (Mat 2:20; 6:33; Rom 11:3), use בעה/בעא for “seek”, which belongs to its own root. בַּקָּשָׁה is given gender f by its form, though BDB heads it n.m. Cognates: Ugaritic bqṯ is cited from Anderson–Moser and Wiktionary only; DULAT (not vendored) and Segert's glossary (which lacks it) not checked for the texts it occurs in. Krahmalkov's page 124 was read from the OCR text, not the scan. Leads not recorded: Oracc Akkadian baqāšu “be broad” (different meaning); Arabic بقس “box tree” (no relation); the link sometimes drawn to Aramaic בחש / Arabic baḥaṯa “search” has a different middle consonant and is not followed. Septuagint renders the noun once by ἀξίωμα (no NT use). Open questions: (1) whether seek-out and seek-yahweh should be one sense with the object distinguishing them; (2) the doctrine items are reasoned conclusions to review.
